standard_prerequisites: Universal models and their finite counterparts: the class U of universal models (every pair of worlds related) and its finite subclass U-Fin, per the frame-definability unit's characterization cited in the statement.

The filtration definition of this unit with its three conditions (defn:filtration and its R-condition, in particular R1: related worlds in M give related classes in M-star) and the finiteness bound prop:filt-are-finite.
The filtration truth lemma (thm:filtrations) transferring satisfaction of formulas in Gamma between a model and its filtration.
core_obligations: A formula A is valid in the class of universal models if and only if it is valid in the class of finite universal models.
Left to right: finite universal models are universal models, so validity over the larger class implies validity over the subclass.

Right to left: if A fails at w in a universal model M, filter M through the subformula set of A; the filtration is finite by the class-count bound, A still fails at the class of w by the truth lemma, and the filtration is itself universal because the universal relation of M forces the R1 condition of the filtration definition for every pair.
proof_roadmap: One-line definitional inclusion for the first direction; for the second, the filtration construction carries the counterexample into a finite model whose universality is re-verified from the definition of the filtration relation.
difficulty_reason: Two-direction argument; the non-trivial direction must combine the truth lemma, the finiteness bound, and the universality preservation through the filtration's R-condition, each applied at the right spot.
